findings.claim: Row r4 has evidence only for the healthy deployment on 0.23.4-1 and the gateway's 302. None of the other six checks is recorded yet - openviking_tools in the gateway log, a viking_search returning lab memories, a transcribed voice note, a medium-reader run through browser_exec, /cron list, a completed dashboard OIDC sign-in - and r4 fails when its evidence is not recorded.

test_apt_installs_jq_but_not_chromium only reads the continuation lines after `apt-get install`, so chromium put back on the install line itself (`--no-install-recommends chromium \`) passes the test. r1 fails_when says chromium is still installed.

entries.change: No code change: the r4 evidence is in, observed by the operator on 2026-11-27 against the live 0.23.4-1 deployment and relayed in direct conversation. A Telegram voice note was transcribed. A memory search returned memories (openviking_tools loaded, viking_search through the sidecar). A Medium link was read through browser_exec; it captured only part of a members-only article, which is the paywall, not the browser. Asked in plain words, the bot listed the scheduled cron jobs; /cron itself is an owner-only terminal command on 0.23.4 and is unknown on Telegram, so the plan's '/cron list' is met through the cron tool instead. Reading /opt/data/SOUL.md worked. The dashboard sign-in through hermes-gateway completed.

test_apt_installs_jq_but_not_chromium now joins continuation lines and reads every apt-get install argument, so chromium on the install line itself fails the test; both mutations (on its own line, and after --no-install-recommends) fail.
Records, per the re-signed eval row r3, that the operator chose no state.db copy and that v0.23.3 moved state.db from schema 31 to 33, so there is no restore point to 0.22.2-3.
